letter.subject: Concern about cookie and tracking practices on https://www.sky.com
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns identified during an automated, passive privacy audit of https://www.sky.com on 2026-11-08 01:55 UTC. The audit used a fresh browser session and recorded what was sent or stored on first visit. No cookie banner was found, so no reject option could be clicked.

Our findings are as follows.

1. Our review suggests that advertising requests ran before any consent choice. Four requests identified as Google advertising activity were sent to googletagmanager.com before the user had answered any cookie banner. No banner was found and no reject action was completed.

2. We observed that an Optimizely cookie was set before any choice could be made. One tracking cookie, optimizelyEndUserId, was already set before the cookie banner was answered.

3. We observed three tracking companies for which we found no mention in the privacy policy reviewed at https://www.sky.com/help/articles/privacy-hub-home. The policy names no companies, and we saw Adobe, Google and Optimizely. We recognise the policy may describe recipients only by category.

4. Our review suggests that the privacy policy is missing several items we expected to find. In the policy reviewed, we did not identify: who is responsible for the processing, the legal basis for using personal data, who it is shared with, and the right to complain to the ICO.

Please would you:

1. Explain each of the points above.
2. Confirm which cookies, trackers and related requests you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential cookies or tracking technologies being set or activated without consent.
4. Reply within one month of this letter.

If there is relevant context we have missed, please include it in your response. If this matter cannot be resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker
